comparator.name: Artificial Intelligence (Kunstmatige Intelligentie)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 programme-specific OER defines a 180-EC bachelor comprising a 135-EC AI major and 45-EC profiling space. The major contains two compulsory 30-EC basic packages, 15 EC of disciplinary requirements, 7.5 EC of experimental methods and statistics, a 7.5-EC thesis, and one formal 45-EC depth package. The normalized target does not choose among the three packages, so the first package in the OER, Learning and Computation, is instantiated by the official-order tie-break. For its two bound-choice slots, the first listed eligible B and C courses are used. The profiling space is preserved without inventing a minor, exchange or internship.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized Kunstmatige Intelligentie target does not select among Utrecht’s three formal 45-EC depth packages. The adopted 2026–2027 OER lists Learning and Computation first, so it is instantiated by official order, before and independently of UCR course selection. Bound choices B and C are represented by the first listed eligible course in each official choice group; the 45-EC profiling space remains open because the OER does not prescribe one subject.

alternatives.label: Artificial Intelligence, Cognition & Intelligent Systems
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible Artificial Intelligence programme combining programming, mathematical reasoning, data, machine learning, neural networks, robotics, decision-making and algorithms with cognition, language, ethics, experimental methods and human-centred communication.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum integrates computational AI with substantial cognitive-science and intelligent-systems study, so the label names all three organising elements.
progression: Programming, mathematics, data, brain-and-behaviour and research foundations precede advanced algorithms, optimisation, deep learning, robotics, cognition and psycholinguistics. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Learning, Computational AI & Autonomous Systems
alternatives.concept: A learning-and-computation route centred on programming, algorithms, software, mathematical and statistical modelling, machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, optimisation, robotics, computer vision, databases, networks and autonomous agents.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum’s dense programming, algorithms, mathematics, machine-learning, optimisation and robotics sequence directly develops Utrecht’s Learning and Computation direction while extending it toward autonomous systems.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match and the cognitive route, this curriculum replaces much of the psychology, neuroscience and philosophy content with databases, networks, software development, advanced algorithms, reinforcement learning and numerical methods.
progression: Research, mathematics, data and database foundations precede programming-intensive software, robotics, algorithms, optimisation, reinforcement learning and deep learning. Programming and Mathematical Methods precede every course that formally requires them, and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Reasoning, Language & Cognitive Systems
alternatives.concept: A reasoning-and-computation route combining logic, algorithms, programming, machine learning and mathematics with language, cognition, neuroscience and philosophy of mind.
alternatives.labelReason: Logic, algorithms, philosophy and language are combined with computational and cognitive-science foundations, making the programme a feasible interdisciplinary response to Utrecht’s Reasoning and Computation package.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad and computational alternatives, this route gives substantially greater weight to neurobiology, lifespan and social psychology, perception, higher cognition, psycholinguistics, philosophy of mind, agency and advanced behavioural research.
progression: Brain-and-behaviour, neurobiology, mathematics, programming and statistical foundations precede perception, higher cognition, psycholinguistics, deep learning, computer vision, algorithms and advanced research. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

selection.assessment: The broad Artificial Intelligence response owns all eight direct programme interests. Utrecht’s three formal 45-EC depth packages then provide independently evidenced related directions. Learning and Computation and Reasoning and Computation each support a distinct feasible UCR curriculum; the Cognitive Processing package is assessed but production stops because three UCR alternatives is the permitted maximum.

notes.text: Utrecht’s Artificial Intelligence bachelor provides a tightly integrated 180-EC sequence across five contributing disciplines, including dedicated formal and natural languages, language models, automated reasoning, knowledge representation and computational language processing. UCR can assemble strong interdisciplinary AI pathways with substantial programming, algorithms, data, learning, robotics, cognition, ethics and research, but it does not reproduce that complete specialist sequence or Utrecht’s fixed depth-package structure.
